Rashi on Sotah 48b:10:1.hebrew: דברים ככתבן - כמשמען, אבן שלמה מסע — כמה שהסיעה מן ההר, ולא סיתתוה שוב בכלי ברזל:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:10:1.english: Words as they are written - According to their literal meaning: "whole stone from the quarry" — just as it was quarried from the mountain, and they did not chisel it again with an iron tool.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:11:1.english: And is it not already stated: "sawed with a saw, etc."?

Rashi on Sotah 48b:12:1.hebrew: שמיר למאי אתא - דאמרי' במס' גיטין (דף סח.) שהביאו שמיר ע"י אשמדאי מלכא דשדאי:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:12:1.english: For what [purpose] did the shamir come - For we say in Tractate Gittin (68a) that they brought the shamir via Ashmedai, king of the demons.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:12:2.english: These stones - [Those] that [were] in the ephod and breastplate.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:12:3.english: Engravings of a signet - [This] implies engraving.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:12:4.hebrew: במלואותם - שיהיו שלמות, שלא יחסרו מהם כלום:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:12:4.english: In their full settings - That they should be complete, [so] that nothing be missing from them.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:13:1.english: And he shows them [the] shamir - [Passing it] over the surface of the ink, like the groove of the letter.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:14:1.hebrew: איטני של אבר - גובתא, מש"א (יש"א: ארגז) בלע"ז:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:14:1.english: A leaden vessel [itenei] - A tube, masha (some say: a chest) in Old French.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:15:1.english: Shira peranda - It is a type of silk.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:16:1.hebrew: סלת צפה על גבי נפה - מרוב שומנה מדבקת בדופני נפה, ודומים לעיסה חיה שנילושה ביין כו'. נופת — דבק הנפה, צופים — שצפה:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:16:1.english: Fine flour that floats on the top of the sieve - Because of its great richness, [the flour] sticks to the sides of the sieve, and [its particles] resemble raw dough that was kneaded with wine, etc. [The word] nofet [refers to] that which sticks to the sieve [nafah], and [the word] tzufim [refers to] that which floats [tzafah].

Rashi on Sotah 48b:16:2.hebrew: שתי ככרות הנדבקות כו' - שהיתה ברכה מצויה בעיסה, וכשמדבקין ככרות בדופני התנור — אחת בדופן זה ואחת בדופן זה שכנגדו — והן תפוחות, אצפליי"ר (להתנפח) בלע"ז, עד שמגעת פני זו לזו. כצוף זה שגדל ומתפשט והולך ותולה באויר, כן אלו צפות ותפוחות באויר:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:16:2.english: Two loaves stuck [in the oven], etc. - For there was a blessing present in the dough, and when they stick loaves to the walls of the oven — one on this wall and one on the wall opposite it — they swell, etzpelier (to swell) in Old French, until the surface of one reaches the other. Just like a honeycomb [tzuf] that grows and spreads continuously and hangs in the air, so too these float [tzafot] and swell in the air.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:16:3.english: From the lookouts [tzofim] - The high mountains from which one looks out into the distance.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:16:4.english: What does it indicate - From where do you learn that honey comes from the mountains?

Rashi on Sotah 48b:16:5.english: As Rav Yosef translates - [The verse:] "As the bees do" [Deuteronomy 1:44].

Rashi on Sotah 48b:17:1.hebrew: כל הנצוק - המערה מכלי טהור לכלי טמא, אין הקילוח מצרפן להיות חיבור לטמא את מה שבתוך הכלי שהוא מערה ממנו:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:17:1.english: Anything that is poured - [When] one pours from a ritually pure vessel into a ritually impure vessel, the stream does not join them to be a connection to render impure that which is inside the vessel from which he is pouring.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:17:2.hebrew: חוץ מדבש זיפין - שהוא עב מאד, והרי הוא כמחובר, שכשהקילוח פוסק, הוא הולך מלמטה למעלה, והכי אמרינן במדות:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:17:2.english: Except for zifin honey - For it is very thick, and behold, it is like [something] connected, for when the stream stops, it goes from below to above, and so we say in [Tractate] Middot.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:17:3.hebrew: הצפחת - ברשק"א בלע"ז, שהן עבות ונכנסת השעוה עם הדבש:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:17:3.english: Hatzapachat [honeycomb] - Bresche in Old French [honeycomb], for they are thick and the wax goes in with the honey.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:17:4.hebrew: שמזייפין בו - מתוך שהוא טוב ועב, מערבין בו מים ויין, ואין נכרות בו:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:17:4.english: That they adulterate it - Because it is good and thick, they mix water and wine into it, and they are not noticeable in it.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:19:1.english: Who believe in the Holy One, Blessed be He - [That is,] to freely spend their money for the beautification [and] enhancement of a mitzvah, and for charity, and for the expenses of Sabbaths and festivals.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:1:1.hebrew: הרחיבה שאול נפשה - לאחר שהביאו חמש פורעניות הללו לעולם, סופן נופלין בגיהנם:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:1:1.english: The netherworld has enlarged her desire - After they have brought these five calamities upon the world, their end [is that] they fall into Gehinnom.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:20:1.hebrew: שיתבזו שולחנם לעתיד לבא - שאין מקבלין שכר שלם, והכי משמע: כי מי בז ליום הבא את הצדיקים:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:20:1.english: That their table will be plundered in the future - For they do not receive a complete reward. And this is what [the verse] implies: For who has plundered the righteous for the coming day?

Rashi on Sotah 48b:20:3.english: The small [children] of the wicked of the children of Israel - Who died while they were young.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:2:1.hebrew: זימנין סליק - פעמים עולים בידם, שנענים, ופעמים שלא עלה בידם; שהרי כשברח דוד מפני אבשלום יצא מירושלים, שאל צדוק באורים ותומים ועלתה לו — שהשיבוהו — ושאל אביתר ולא עלתה לו, שנאמר: "ויעל אביתר" — שנסתלק מן הכהונה מפני שלא נענה באורים ותומים. והכי תניא בסדר עולם גבי ארון: "ובברחו מפני אבשלום יצא עמו עד שעלה במעלה הזיתים, ונשאל באורים ותומים, ונסתלק אביתר מן הכהונה גדולה, נכנס צדוק תחתיו, כדכתיב (שמואל ב ט״ו:כ״ה) ויאמר המלך לצדוק השב את הארון וגו'":
Rashi on Sotah 48b:2:1.english: [There were] times it rose up - Sometimes they succeeded, in that they were answered, and sometimes they did not succeed; for when David fled from Absalom [and] went out from Jerusalem, Tzadok inquired of the Urim VeTummim and it rose up for him — [in that] they answered him — and Abiathar inquired and it did not rise up for him, as it is stated: "And Abiathar went up" — [meaning] that he was removed from the priesthood because he was not answered through the Urim VeTummim. And so it is taught in Seder Olam regarding the Ark: "And when he fled from Absalom, [the Ark] went out with him until he ascended the ascent of the Mount of Olives, and he inquired of the Urim VeTummim, and Abiathar was removed from the high priesthood, [and] Tzadok entered in his place, as it is written (II Samuel 15:25): 'And the king said to Tzadok: Return the Ark, etc.'"

Rashi on Sotah 48b:3:1.english: In the days of Zechariah - And he was the son of Jehoiada, who was in the days of Joash.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:4:1.english: Cities with fields - The cities of the Levites, upon which Scripture imposed [the requirement of] open fields.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:5:1.english: Until there stood a priest, etc. - Thus, there were Urim [VeTummim] in the Second Temple.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:5:2.hebrew: אמור לו - לא שהיו אורים ותומים, אלא כאדם שאומר לחבירו כו'. אלמא כל ימי המקדש ראשון הוו:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:5:2.english: Say to him - Not that there were Urim VeTummim, rather [it is] like a person who says to his friend, etc. Thus, they existed all the days of the First Temple.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:6:1.english: As it was taught [in a baraita] - Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi are called latter [prophets].

Rashi on Sotah 48b:9:1.hebrew: שמעון וישמעאל - רבן שמעון שהיה נשיא, ורבי ישמעאל בן אלישע כהן גדול, שהרגתם מלכות יון:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:9:1.english: Shimon and Yishmael - Rabban Shimon, who was [the] Nasi, and Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha, [the] High Priest, whom the kingdom of Greece killed.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:9:2.english: For the sword - [Meaning] that they are destined to be killed by the sword.

Rashi on Sotah 48b:9:3.hebrew: לקטלא - לשאר מיתות, כגון רבי עקיבא שסרקו בשרו במסריקות פיפיות של ברזל כדאמר בברכות (דף סא:), ור' חנניה בן תרדיון שנשרף, ורבי יהודה בן בבא בלונביאות של ברזל כדאמר בסנהדרין (דף יד.):
Rashi on Sotah 48b:9:3.english: For killing - [This refers] to other [forms of] death, such as Rabbi Akiva, whose flesh they combed with toothed iron combs, as it says in Berakhot (61b), and Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon, who was burned, and Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava, [who was killed] with iron spears, as it says in Sanhedrin (14a).

Rashi on Sotah 48b:9:4.hebrew: שאין מספידין על הרוגי מלכות - מאימת המלך, לפיכך מיחו בידם:
Rashi on Sotah 48b:9:4.english: For they do not eulogize those killed by the monarchy - Out of fear of the king; therefore they prevented them [from doing so].
